symptoms.label: Blisters or ulcers in the mouth
Blisters or wounds on the hoof
Firm lumps / nodules on the skin
Ulcers on the tongue or gums

diseases.name: Foot and Mouth Disease (FMD)
diseases.definition: A highly contagious viral disease of cloven-hoofed animals causing blisters in the mouth and on the feet.
diseases.causes: Foot-and-mouth disease virus (an Aphthovirus), spread very easily between animals.
diseases.transmission: Direct contact, contaminated feed, water, equipment, vehicles, and airborne spread over short distances.
diseases.prevention: Regular vaccination, quarantine of new animals, strict farm hygiene and movement control during outbreaks.
diseases.treatment_overview: Supportive care only; there is no specific cure. Soft feed, wound care and rest help recovery. Antibiotics are sometimes used by a vet to prevent secondary infection.
diseases.diet: Soft, palatable feed (green fodder, gruel), plenty of clean water, avoid rough dry fodder while mouth lesions heal.
diseases.supportive_care: Isolate the animal, clean mouth and foot lesions with mild antiseptic as advised, keep bedding soft and dry.
diseases.vaccination: Vaccinate every 6 months in endemic regions.

diseases.name: Lumpy Skin Disease (LSD)
diseases.definition: A viral disease of cattle causing firm nodules across the skin, fever and reduced production.
diseases.transmission: Mainly by biting insects (mosquitoes, flies, ticks); also contaminated equipment.
diseases.prevention: Vaccination, insect control, isolation of affected animals.
diseases.treatment_overview: No specific antiviral treatment. Supportive care and wound management; a vet may treat secondary bacterial infection.
diseases.diet: Good-quality green fodder, protein feed, clean water, mineral and vitamin support to aid recovery.
diseases.supportive_care: Clean skin lesions, control flies, provide shade and rest, isolate from the herd.

diseases.name: Mastitis
diseases.definition: Inflammation of the udder, usually from bacterial infection, affecting milk quality and yield.
diseases.causes: Bacteria entering the teat canal, often linked to poor milking hygiene.
diseases.transmission: Environmental and contagious bacteria spread during milking and through contaminated bedding.
diseases.prevention: Clean milking practice, teat dipping, dry-cow management, clean dry bedding.
diseases.treatment_overview: Veterinary treatment of the infection and frequent complete milking. Consult a vet before any medication.
diseases.diet: Balanced ration, green fodder, clean water, adequate energy and minerals.
diseases.supportive_care: Frequent gentle milking of the affected quarter, keep the udder clean, apply warm compress if advised.
diseases.recovery_time: Days to weeks depending on severity.
diseases.vaccination: Some vaccines exist; hygiene is the main control.

diseases.name: Bovine Respiratory Disease (BRD)
diseases.definition: A complex of respiratory infections causing coughing, fever and breathing difficulty, common after stress or transport.
diseases.causes: A mix of viruses and bacteria, often triggered by stress, crowding or cold weather.
diseases.prevention: Reduce stress and crowding, good ventilation, vaccination, gradual weaning/transport.
diseases.treatment_overview: Prompt veterinary treatment. Early care improves outcomes; consult a vet for any medication.
diseases.diet: Palatable feed, clean water, avoid dusty feed, keep the animal warm and rested.
diseases.supportive_care: Good ventilation, dry warm shelter, isolate sick animals, reduce handling stress.

diseases.name: Bloat
diseases.definition: A dangerous build-up of gas in the rumen causing a swollen left flank and breathing distress.
diseases.causes: Sudden access to lush legume pasture or grain, or a blockage preventing gas release.
diseases.prevention: Introduce rich feed gradually, avoid grazing wet legume pasture on an empty stomach.
diseases.treatment_overview: An emergency — contact a veterinarian immediately. Rapid intervention can be life-saving.
diseases.diet: After recovery, reintroduce feed slowly with plenty of fibrous fodder.
diseases.supportive_care: Keep the animal moving and standing, contact a vet without delay.
diseases.recovery_time: Rapid if treated in time; can be fatal within hours if not.

diseases.name: Haemorrhagic Septicaemia (HS)
diseases.definition: A severe, often fatal bacterial disease of cattle and buffalo, common in the monsoon season.
diseases.transmission: Ingestion or inhalation; stress and wet weather increase risk.
diseases.prevention: Annual vaccination before the monsoon, good nutrition, reduce stress.
diseases.treatment_overview: A veterinary emergency needing immediate treatment; early antibiotics by a vet can save the animal.
diseases.diet: Supportive nutrition and clean water during recovery.
diseases.supportive_care: Isolate, keep dry and warm, seek veterinary help immediately.
diseases.recovery_time: Guarded; depends on how early it is treated.
diseases.vaccination: Vaccinate annually before the rainy season.

diseases.name: Viral Diarrhea / Enteritis
diseases.definition: Intestinal infection causing persistent diarrhea, dehydration and weight loss.
diseases.transmission: Contaminated feed, water and faecal-oral spread.
diseases.prevention: Clean water and feed, good sanitation, vaccination where available.
diseases.treatment_overview: Rehydration and veterinary care. Consult a vet, especially if diarrhea persists.
diseases.diet: Electrolytes and clean water, easily digestible feed, avoid sudden feed changes.
diseases.supportive_care: Provide oral electrolytes/hydration, isolate, keep clean and dry.
diseases.recovery_time: Days to a couple of weeks with good hydration.

diseases.name: Ketosis
diseases.definition: A metabolic disorder in early-lactation dairy animals from negative energy balance.
diseases.causes: Energy demand of milk production exceeding feed intake after calving.
diseases.prevention: Good transition-period nutrition, adequate energy in early lactation, avoid over-fat cows at calving.
diseases.treatment_overview: Veterinary management of energy balance. Consult a vet for treatment.
diseases.diet: Energy-dense, palatable ration; ensure the animal keeps eating; clean water.
diseases.supportive_care: Encourage feed intake, reduce stress, monitor closely.

diseases.name: Milk Fever (Hypocalcemia)
diseases.definition: A sudden drop in blood calcium around calving, causing weakness and inability to stand.
diseases.causes: Calcium demand of milk production at calving outpacing calcium mobilisation.
diseases.prevention: Correct calcium/phosphorus balance in the transition diet, veterinary guidance around calving.
diseases.treatment_overview: A veterinary emergency; prompt treatment is usually very effective. Contact a vet immediately.
diseases.diet: Balanced minerals; follow veterinary advice on calcium around calving.
diseases.supportive_care: Keep the animal comfortable and upright, seek veterinary help without delay.

diseases.name: Gastrointestinal Parasites (Worms)
diseases.definition: Internal worm burden causing gradual weight loss, poor coat and sometimes diarrhea.
diseases.causes: Roundworms and other internal parasites picked up from pasture.
diseases.transmission: Ingestion of larvae from contaminated pasture.
diseases.prevention: Strategic deworming, pasture rotation, avoid overgrazing.
diseases.treatment_overview: Deworming under veterinary guidance and improved nutrition. Consult a vet for the right product and timing.
diseases.diet: Good-quality fodder, protein and mineral supplementation to restore condition.
diseases.supportive_care: Improve nutrition, keep pasture clean, monitor body condition.
diseases.vaccination: Generally none; deworming programmes are used.

diseases.name: Bovine Tuberculosis
diseases.definition: A slow, chronic bacterial disease of cattle causing progressive wasting and a persistent cough.
diseases.transmission: Inhaled droplets between animals in close contact; also via contaminated feed and unpasteurised milk.
diseases.prevention: Regular testing and removal of reactors, quarantine of new animals, good ventilation and hygiene.
diseases.treatment_overview: Treatment is generally not attempted in livestock; control is by testing and removal under veterinary and government programmes. It is a notifiable zoonotic disease in many regions — contact a veterinarian.
diseases.diet: Good-quality nutrition to maintain condition while under veterinary supervision.
diseases.supportive_care: Isolate suspected animals and contact a veterinarian immediately; avoid consuming raw milk.
diseases.recovery_time: Chronic; animals typically do not recover without intervention.
diseases.vaccination: Not routinely used in cattle in most regions; control relies on testing.

diseases.name: Bluetongue
diseases.definition: An insect-borne viral disease, most severe in sheep, causing fever, mouth ulcers and lameness.
diseases.transmission: Bites from Culicoides midges; not spread by direct contact.
diseases.prevention: Vaccination where available, midge control, housing animals during peak midge activity.
diseases.treatment_overview: No specific antiviral treatment; supportive care and veterinary management of secondary infection.
diseases.diet: Soft palatable feed and clean water while mouth lesions heal.
diseases.supportive_care: Shade, rest, soft bedding, insect control, wound care as advised by a vet.
diseases.recovery_time: Several weeks in animals that recover; can be fatal in sheep.
diseases.vaccination: Serotype-specific vaccines are available in some regions.

diseases.name: Johne's Disease (Paratuberculosis)
diseases.definition: A chronic intestinal bacterial infection causing persistent diarrhoea and steady weight loss despite a normal appetite.
diseases.transmission: Faecal-oral, usually infected as calves via contaminated milk, water or bedding.
diseases.prevention: Clean calving areas, feed calves clean colostrum/milk, cull known infected animals, test herds.
diseases.treatment_overview: There is no effective cure; management focuses on control and culling. Consult a veterinarian for herd-level planning.
diseases.diet: High-quality, easily digestible feed to slow condition loss.
diseases.supportive_care: Isolate affected animals from young stock, maintain hygiene, seek veterinary advice.
diseases.recovery_time: Chronic and progressive; recovery is not expected.
diseases.vaccination: Available in some regions but restricted.

diseases.name: Caprine Arthritis Encephalitis (CAE)
diseases.definition: A chronic viral disease of goats causing swollen joints and lameness in adults, and nervous signs in kids.
diseases.transmission: Mainly through infected colostrum and milk to kids; also close contact.
diseases.prevention: Feed kids heat-treated colostrum, test and separate infected animals, cull positives.
diseases.treatment_overview: No cure; management is supportive and focused on comfort. A veterinarian can advise on pain management and herd control.
diseases.diet: Easily reachable feed and water, good nutrition to maintain condition.
diseases.supportive_care: Soft bedding, easy access to feed and water, minimise walking distance for lame goats.
diseases.vaccination: None available; control is by management.

diseases.name: Scrapie
diseases.definition: A fatal degenerative disease of the nervous system in sheep and goats, causing intense rubbing, incoordination and wasting.
diseases.transmission: Mainly from ewe to lamb around birth and via a contaminated environment.
diseases.prevention: Source replacement stock from scrapie-free flocks, breed for resistant genotypes, strict lambing hygiene.
diseases.treatment_overview: There is no treatment or cure. It is a notifiable disease in many regions — report suspected cases to a veterinarian.
diseases.supportive_care: Isolate and contact a veterinarian; the condition is always fatal.
